title: Why banjo and tuba came back in the 1933 band
summary: Asked why the rhythm section returned to banjo and tuba, Randolph thinks it was McKendrick's idea.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: There was a change in that band musically that I'm puzzled about. And the '31 band, Mike McKendrick, on the records, at least, is playing guitar, it sounds like. And in the '33 band, he's playing banjo, and Bill Oldham sometimes is playing tuba, which is like a throwback to the '20s.
Because the banjo and tuba were -- by that time, most of the bands had switched to string bass and guitar. But why the banjo, particularly, and the tuba on some things?
Well, let's see, Bill Oldham did have a tuba, I believe. But he didn't have it in the '34 band. See, I had the Oldham boys in that last band, too.
Oh, But in the '33 bands, on the records, sometimes he plays tuba, but most of the time he plays string bass.
But sometimes he's playing tuba and it's an older sound, and I just wonder -- was it Louis' idea to do that, or was it yours, or why? Why go back to banjo, once you had guitar?
No, I think it was -- I think just
Mike wanted to do that, probably, because I didn't bother him too much about that.
No, I didn't bother him. It was just -- yeah, that's right. I think that's probably Mike's idea.
